decision_reason: A1 leaves the low-U_NN pair standing still versus lying down distinguished only by one global posture coordinate, while lying down and jump front & back also have the weakest seen-prototype coverage. Splitting posture inclination by instrumented body segment adds observable posture evidence, and gravity-axis translation gives jump front & back a transferable contrast with running using climbing stairs as a seen anchor. An ankle-scoped impact attribute further distinguishes walking from faster or more impact-heavy locomotion without duplicating global motion intensity. The constant A1 motion_regularity coordinate provides no class discrimination in this split and is removed.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: trunk_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the trunk, represented by the instrumented chest, within a window.

levels.Low: Trunk is nearly upright relative to gravity.
levels.Medium: Trunk is moderately inclined relative to gravity.
levels.High: Trunk is strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: lower_limb_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the instrumented lower-limb segment at the left ankle within a window.

levels.Low: Instrumented lower-limb segment is nearly upright relative to gravity.
levels.Medium: Instrumented lower-limb segment is moderately inclined relative to gravity.
levels.High: Instrumented lower-limb segment is strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: gravity_axis_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of repeated whole-body translational motion along the gravity axis, independent of sustained horizontal progression.

levels.Low: Little or no repeated translation along the gravity axis.
levels.Medium: Moderate repeated translation along the gravity axis.
levels.High: Prominent repeated upward-and-downward translation along the gravity axis.

attributes.name: ankle_impact
attributes.definition: Degree of short-duration impact or abrupt acceleration localized at the instrumented ankle.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced ankle-localized impact peaks.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains a broad, physically supported separator between static postures, walking, and vigorous locomotion, with jogging and running providing seen transfer anchors.
Repetition rate supplies a rate-specific contrast not contained in motion magnitude and transfers from seen cyclic activities such as cycling, jogging, and running.
Sustained rapid fluctuation is physically distinct from isolated impacts and helps contrast jump front & back with smoother repeated movements using running and waist bends forward as seen anchors.
Global short-duration peaks remain important for separating jump front & back from static or smooth activities, with running providing a seen high-impact anchor.

The original global inclination compresses independently observable chest and ankle orientations. Segmenting it provides additional gravity-relative evidence for the close standing still versus lying down pair and supports transfer through sitting and relaxing and articulated seen postures.

Temporal change in global posture is distinct from average segment inclination and helps separate posture-changing jump front & back from stable standing still and lying down, with knees bending (crouching) as a seen anchor.
Angular-motion prominence remains independent of linear progression and is transferable from seen limb- and trunk-rotation activities to locomotor classes.
Sustained locomotor progression separates walking from stationary postures and distinguishes progressing gait from bounded front-and-back jumping, with jogging and climbing stairs as seen anchors.

The supplied A1 prototypes assign High motion_regularity to every seen and unseen activity, so the coordinate contributes no split-specific contrast. Cadence continues to represent repetition rate without retaining this constant dimension.

Gravity-aligned translation separates the strongly upward-and-downward structure of jump front & back from primarily progressive walking and running. Climbing stairs and knees bending (crouching) provide seen support for vertical body motion.

Localizing abrupt peaks to the ankle adds a transferable gait-contact distinction beyond global impulsiveness, helping distinguish walking from more impact-heavy jogging, running, and jump front & back.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final attributes retain distinct physical roles: motion_intensity measures total energy; cadence measures repetition rate; smoothness measures sustained rapid change; impulsiveness measures global isolated peaks; ankle_impact measures the location-specific impact component; trunk_inclination and lower_limb_inclination measure separate segment orientations; posture_variability measures temporal posture change; rotational_motion measures angular prominence; translational_motion measures sustained progression; and gravity_axis_translation isolates the gravity-aligned component of translation. The scoped ankle-impact attribute is intentionally related to, but not interchangeable with, global impulsiveness. Gravity-axis translation is a directional decomposition rather than a duplicate of overall translational progression. The nondiscriminative A1 motion_regularity dimension is removed.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
